[ERROR LIST]
 Line 2122: Redundant duplicate entry "Sexual content" on consecutive lines within SYSTEM_PROMPT.
 Line 5253: Flawed condition and misleading HTTP status code/message: when length < 1 (e.g., 0 or negative), the handler raises HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE (413) with the message "Request body is too large." instead of rejecting an empty or invalid body with HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST (400).
 Line 55 / Line 96: Missing roottype validation on parsed JSON: read_json can return any valid JSON value (such as a list, string, or integer). Line 96 then calls payload.get("messages"), causing an unhandled AttributeError instead of raising an ApiError with a 400 Bad Request status.
 Line 141142 / Line 219224: Premature stream termination: extract_delta returns (None, True) when raw_event is empty. If an upstream server sends an empty SSE data ping or keepalive (e.g., data: or data: ), event_payload evaluates to "", causing line 223 (if finished: break) to abruptly terminate the stream before receiving [DONE].
 Line 165166: Dummy/stub method: log_message is overridden with an empty passthrough (return) that completely silences server access and error logs.
 Line 178, 181, 197: Flawed routing path inspection: self.path retains raw query strings (e.g., /api/health?check=1 or /api/chat?stream=true) without URL parsing or normalization, causing requests containing query parameters to fail with HTTP 404 Not Found.
 Line 225: Resource leak: upstream.close() is not wrapped in a finally block or context manager; any exception raised during the linebyline reading loop bypasses socket cleanup.
 Line 226233: Broken HTTP framing and protocol violation: HTTP headers (HTTP 200 OK, Content-Type: text/event-stream) are committed and flushed at lines 203208. If an exception occurs during the streaming loop (lines 210224), send_json is invoked, attempting to write a second HTTP response status line and headers directly into the active SSE response body.
 Line 243: Potential deadlock: calling server.shutdown() on the main thread after serve_forever() violates the standard library contract for socketserver.BaseServer.shutdown(), which is documented to deadlock if invoked on the same thread as the event loop.
